title: Minkä maalainen: asking about one person's nationality
summary: Minkä maalainen asks what nationality someone is. Minkä maalainen sinä olet? — Olen suomalainen.
targetSkills: Minkä maalainen: asking about one person's nationality
objectives: Ask one person's nationality with minkä maalainen.
Answer with a nationality word and distinguish nationality from residence or origin.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which.
An adjective is a word that describes a quality.

Minkä maalainen asks what nationality someone is. The joined spelling minkämaalainen is also used. A nationality is not automatically the country where someone currently lives or the place they travelled from.
keyPoints: Do not replace the nationality question with a question about current residence.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Reply with a nationality word: Olen suomalainen (“I am Finnish”). Nationality words begin with a lower-case letter, unlike country names such as Suomi (“Finland”). Learn the taught nationality words; do not assume every country name takes the same ending. For these words -lainen/-läinen belongs to the nationality word, not to olla.
A natural short reply to “Minkä maalainen sinä olet?” is “Suomalainen.” (“Finnish.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
Reject a suggested nationality with the complete phrase en ole and then give the actual nationality. A negative reply alone does not establish which nationality the speaker is.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Give the requested nationality word, not a country name or an in-country location.

steps: En: I do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.
ole: be; main verb after the negative verb. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
